passage: Saturday night. Today was my birthday. Gopika promised on Monday and again on Thursday that she would come. I put the balloons up myself and kept the good chair for her. She did not come, and no one called. I kept looking at the door while we cut the cake. Everyone else was there, and Nani kept calling me the birthday girl, but my chest felt heavy. I am not going to snap at her, and I will not stop talking to her either. On Monday I will say, "I felt sad when you did not come. What happened?" I want to know first. Sangeeta.

qa.q: How many times did Gopika promise she would come?
qa.a: Gopika promised on Monday and again on Thursday.

qa.q: What was Sangeeta feeling as she kept looking at the door?
qa.a: She felt hurt and disappointed, and her chest felt heavy even with everyone else at the party.

qa.q: What is Sangeeta's plan for talking with Gopika, and why might it work?
qa.a: She plans to say calmly how she felt and ask what happened. Speaking without snapping gives Gopika a chance to explain and keeps the friendship open. 🙂

qa.q: How might Gopika see Monday's conversation if she had a good reason for missing the party?
qa.a: She may feel relieved that Sangeeta asked rather than accused, and want to explain and apologise.

grounding: A child hurt that her friend missed her birthday plans to tell her calmly what it felt like and ask why.
